summary:
Landing on the Moon's south pole presents major challenges due to extreme shadows, limited solar illumination and interrupted communication with Earth. Even small changes in landing location or mission timing can significantly affect feasibility.

LUNAR is an interactive mission-planning platform that combines NASA/JPL Horizons ephemeris, LOLA terrain data and other lunar datasets to evaluate potential landing sites. It calculates terrain-aware sunlight and Earth visibility, assesses operational requirements and compares sites using a transparent weighted suitability model.

Beyond displaying scientific data, LUNAR introduces an adaptive Mission Rescue Engine that searches alternative landing sites and dates when mission schedules change. Its Opportunity Atlas, multi-objective optimisation and interactive 3D visualisations help users understand mission risks, trade-offs and feasible alternatives.

With dedicated Explorer and Scientist modes, LUNAR makes complex lunar mission analysis accessible to both technical users and the wider public, supporting clearer and more informed exploration decisions.
details:
LUNAR is an interactive mission-planning platform designed to simplify landing-site selection near the Moon's south pole, where extreme shadows, challenging terrain and limited Earth visibility create significant engineering constraints. Using NASA/JPL Horizons, LOLA and other lunar datasets, LUNAR calculates terrain-aware sunlight, communication windows and surface conditions. Its scientific assessment evaluates 15 weighted criteria using an 82-point suitability framework, alongside mandatory mission requirements and evidence coverage indicators. Interactive 3D visualisations, built using Three.js and Blender, allow users to explore lunar terrain and understand how conditions change over time. Dedicated Explorer and Scientist modes make the platform accessible to both the public and technical users.

Beyond displaying scientific data, LUNAR introduces adaptive mission-planning capabilities. Its Mission Rescue Engine searches alternative landing sites and dates when mission schedules change, while the Opportunity Atlas and Decision Laboratory provide site comparisons, Pareto optimisation and sensitivity analysis. Simplified power and communication simulations help evaluate operational risks. Scientific calculations are checked against independent reference data, with assumptions and limitations clearly documented. By combining NASA data, explainable decision-making and interactive visualisation, LUNAR aims to make lunar mission planning more efficient, accessible and adaptable.
